# What is vision for?

## Information at a distance

![James Webb space telescope deep field @noauthor_undated-vq](https://stsci-opo.org/STScI-01G7DCYVZ899DGSY684E801B2Y.png){#fig-web-deep-field width="70%"}

## Nature's speed demon/speed limit

- Light (+ radiowaves) circumnavigate the Earth in ~133 ms

![https://w3tm.org](https://w3tm.org/posts/2024-07-12-summertime/kc3bhi-w3swl-km4aj.jpeg){width="35%" #fig-field-day-2025-w3tm}

- Earth ~8.3 light-minutes from the Sun

## Where is it/am I?

::: {.incremental}
- Azimuth (left/right)
- Elevation (up/down)
- Distance (near/far)
- Orientation
:::

## What is it?

::: {.incremental}
- Edges $\rightarrow$
- Surfaces $\rightarrow$
- Objects or entities
:::

## Regarding data figures...

- *What* are the figure components
  - Data points, text, bars/segments/rings/boxes
- *Where* are different components relative to one another, axes, etc.
- *How* do figure components convey information about data?
  - Bar heights = or not
  - Scatterplot points clustered or not
  
---

```{r}
#| label: fig-ice-cream-sample-ratings
#| fig-cap: "Some sample ratings of ice cream flavors."
library(ggplot2)
library(dplyr)
library(forcats)
flavors <- c("vanilla", "chocolate", "strawberry", "mocha")
ratings <- c(5, 4.9, 4.7, 3)
ice_cream <- data.frame(flavor = flavors, rating = ratings)

ice_cream |>
  mutate(flavor = fct_rev(fct_reorder(flavor, rating))) |>
  
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = flavor, y = rating, fill = flavor) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity") +
  theme_classic() +
  theme(legend.position = "none")
```

---

```{r}
#| label: fig-random-xy-sd-1.25
#| fig-cap: "Some sample data where $x = y + N(0, 1.25)$."
x = runif(n = 100, min = -1, max = 1)
y = x + rnorm(n = 100, mean = 0, sd = 1.25)
points_df <- data.frame(x = x, y = y)

points_df |>
  ggplot() +
  aes(x = x, y = y) +
  geom_point() +
  theme(aspect.ratio = 1) +
  theme_classic()
```

# Detecting information in light

## What information?

- Position
- Length
- Area
- Color
- Texture
- (Motion)

## The eye

![](https://hmslade5.files.wordpress.com/2012/03/anatomy-of-the-eye.jpg){fig-align="center" #fig-the-eye}

## is like an auto-focus, auto-exposure camera...

![](https://www.optilase.com/wp-content/uploads/2014/12/camera-lens-eye-lens.jpg){#fig-eye-autofocus-camera fig-align="center"}

## part of a self-stabilizing system...

{{< video https://www.youtube.com/embed/JGArTWOJtXs?start=7 width="100%" height="70%" class="center_img">}}

@Bucalo2015-qm

## Eye + head + body system

::: {.callout-note}
- Eye + head + body movements *align and point* the eyes
- Eye + head + body movements *stabilize* the eyes
  - When the observer moves
  - When objects move
:::

## Demo

- May I have a volunteer?

## Image formation

- Eye's optical components
  - Cornea (fixed refraction)
  - Iris/pupil (*modifiable* aperture)
  - Lens (*modifiable* refraction) 
- Create projection (image) on retina

## The retina...

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- samples spatial patterns of light intensity & wavelength
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](https://www.feinberg.northwestern.edu/gfx/news/retina.jpg){fig-align="center" #fig-the-retina}
:::
::::

## 'Wavelength-tuned' photoreceptors

![Wikipedia^[By BenRG - Own work, Public Domain, https://commons.wikimedia.org/w/index.php?curid=7873848]](https://thumb.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/thumb/0/04/Cone-fundamentals-with-srgb-spectrum.svg/3840px-Cone-fundamentals-with-srgb-spectrum.svg.png?utm_source=en.wikipedia.org&utm_campaign=imageinfo&utm_content=thumbnail){#fig-cone-photoreceptors width="60%"}

---

![Retinal rods (green) & cones (blue)](https://i.pinimg.com/originals/9f/08/85/9f0885d4c209d5275f631ac194eb4f4b.jpg){#fig-rods-cones}

---

### ...arranged in mosaics

![Normal color vision vs. protanopic (color blind) vision; Source: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Retinal_mosaic](https://upload.wikimedia.org/wikipedia/commons/a/a6/ConeMosaics.jpg){#fig-cone-rod-mosaics}

---

### with different concentrations in different parts of the retina

![https://book.bionumbers.org/how-big-is-a-photoreceptor/](https://book.bionumbers.org/wp-content/uploads/2014/07/130-f2-RodCellDensity-12.png){#fig-book-bionumbers}

## Consequences

- Must move eyes in order to position highest resolution part of retina over target
- Keep track of sequence of eye movements and positions over time
- Integrate sequence of samples over time

---

![@Cairo2013-hm Figure 5.6](../include/img/cairo-fig-5.6.png)

## Information processing

- Separate channels for short, medium, long wavelengths (cones): chromatic (color)
- Black/gray/white or overall illumination (rods): achromatic (dark/light)
- ~120 M rods + ~ 5 M cones (125 M) vs. professional cameras with 100 M pixels

---

- Point by point, topographic (map-like) 2D image of 3D world
- Non-uniform resolution (center >> periphery)
- yields focused image except...

---

### ...when eye misshapen for cornea  +lens

- Grating acuity
- Vernier
- Symbol/letter (optotype) acuity

## Contrast sensitivity

- Light/dark ratio (contast)
- vs. spatial frequency (level of detail)
- Contrast -> edges; edges -> shape/form
- e.g., driving in fog

---

![Contrast sensitivity function](https://www.psychophysics.uk/wp-content/uploads/2019/04/typical-contrast-sensitivity-function.jpg)

## {.scrollable}

![Pelli-Robson Contrast Sensitivity Chart](https://precision-vision.com/cdn/shop/files/5014_1-scaled-1.jpg?v=1776157164&width=1400){#fig-pelli-robson width="80%"}

## Color perception

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Perceived color a function of activity in "R", "G", and "B" photoreceptors
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/colcon.html](http://hyperphysics.phy-astr.gsu.edu/hbase/vision/imgvis/colcon.png){#fig-color-perception}
:::
::::

## Wavelengths are continuous, but are perceived colors?

![https://rmit.pressbooks.pub/colourtheory1/part/2-colour-theory-the-visible-spectrum/](https://rmit.pressbooks.pub/app/uploads/sites/42/2022/10/visitble-spectrum-nm.png)

## Perceived colors seem ordinal, but...

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Order "wraps" around the spectrum
- Color is a neuropsychological construct
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![](https://cdn.pixabay.com/photo/2013/07/12/19/20/rainbow-colors-154569_1280.png){#fig-color-wheel}
:::
::::

## Color vision anomalies

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=50%}
- Absence of or anomalies in photoreceptors
:::
::: {.column width=50%}
![https://bluefinvision.com/ishihara-colour-blind-test-online/](https://bluefinvision.com/wp-content/uploads/2025/02/eye-tests-ishihara-colour-blind-test.webp){#fig-ishihara width="55%"}
:::
::::

## Types

:::: {.columns}
::: {.column width=40%}
- Protanopia (impaired R/long wavelength)
- Deuteranopia (impaired G/medium wavelength)
- Tritanopia (impaired B/short wavelength)
:::
::: {.column width=60%}
![https://www.color-blindness.com/protanopia-red-green-color-blindness/](https://www.color-blindness.com/wp-content/images/Protanopia-Color-Spectrum.jpg){#fig-color-vision-anomolies}
:::
::::

## Some consequences for data figures

- Size of visual elements (symbols, including text)
- Contrast (light/dark or color)
- Textures of visual patterns
- Some colors more visible than others
  - [Vischeck](https://www.vischeck.com/)
- How much visual scanning (# of eye movements)?

# Wrap-up

## Main points

- Visual perception a *reconstruction* of reality
- Continuous pattern of light $\rightarrow$ intensity detected by 4 photoreceptor types
- Retina has non-uniform sensivity to light, so some information more easily detected
- Basic knowledge of vision can help generate better data visualizations
